newsitem.title: USA: General Acceptance to post 1996 Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: General Acceptance to post 1996 Q4 loss.

text.p: General Acceptance Corp said Friday it will report a loss for the 1996 fourth quarter when its results are released in late March.

It attributed the loss to a provision for credit losses to be recorded as a result of higher-than-anticipated fourth-quarter chargeoffs and, to a lesser extent, to a seasonal reduction in revenue at the company's vehicle sales outlets.
General Acceptance said it is still determining an appropriate level of reserves for credit losses.

The company has been operating under the terms of a forbearance agreement with its primary lender. It said the agreement, as last amended, has been extended through March 31, 1997 at an interest rate of LIBOR plus 4.00 percent.
Meanwhile, General Acceptance said it has completed the sale of $14.5 million of installment sale contracts, which generated net proceeds of $13.2 million.
In addition, it said it completed two smaller sales of a total of $4.1 million in installment sale contracts -- also on a non-recourse basis -- for total cash proceeds of $4.2 million.

Because these investment sale contracts were sold essentially at their carrying value, the company said it does not anticipate recording any gain or loss associated with their sale. Proceeds were used to reduce debt.

It plans to make similar additional sales as part of its interim funding strategy, due, in part, to significant delays in its securitization plans. It said it cannot estimate now the date when it can complete a securitization.
General Acceptance is a specialized consumer finance company that buys and services installment sale contracts on used cars to consumers with limited access to traditional financing.
